headline: ANGLOGOLD PAYS C$58.5M TO DOUBLE THESIS GOLD STAKE — 9.7% OWNERSHIP OF LAWYERS-RANCH CLOSES AUG. 27
snippet: AngloGold Ashanti (NYSE: AU) is investing C$58.5 million to lift its stake in Thesis Gold & Silver (TSXV: TAU) from approximately 5% to 9.7% — doubling down on the Lawyers-Ranch gold-silver project in British Columbia just months after its initial C$38.7 million entry in February 2026. The deal comprises C$28.5 million in common shares (8.34 million shares) and C$30 million in flow-through shares to fund eligible Canadian exploration expenditures at Lawyers-Ranch, with closing expected around August 27 subject to TSX Venture Exchange approval. AngloGold is funding Thesis as the company advances a feasibility study on Lawyers-Ranch — due in 2027 — while carrying out exploration and permitting work. A senior miner buying two tranches within six months at a TSX-V junior is a strong endorsement of the project's development trajectory: AngloGold is not a passive financial investor but a major gold producer signalling that Lawyers-Ranch meets its internal threshold for future acquisition consideration. At $4,400 gold, the NPV backdrop for a British Columbia gold-silver project with a feasibility study in progress is as strong as any point in modern mining history.

headline: NEXMETALS PUSHES SELEBI MAIN CU-NI MASSIVE SULPHIDE TREND TO 1.45KM — MRE UPDATE DUE Q3
snippet: NexMetals Mining (TSXV: NEXM) reported August 17 that drill hole SMD-26-219 at the Selebi Main deposit in Botswana intersected multiple intervals of semi-massive and massive sulphide mineralization — extending the high-grade mineralized trend by approximately 450 metres beyond previous drilling, for a total interpreted strike length of roughly 1.45 kilometres. The visual intercepts include a 20.0-metre Main Zone interval and a 7.55-metre Lower Zone hit including 6.60 metres dominated by massive sulphides. All of this extension lies outside NexMetals' 2024 Mineral Resource Estimate, meaning the coming Q3 2026 resource update is being fed by genuine step-out discoveries rather than infill conversion. The drill result builds on the company's best assayed hole to date — SMD-26-212-W1, which returned 11.15 metres at 7.65% CuEq (3.10% Cu, 2.21% Ni) from the 30,000-metre 2026 program. Copper-nickel-cobalt systems with kilometre-scale massive sulphide trends and resource updates imminent represent exactly the combination that triggers institutional attention in a copper market where LME spot is trading $545/tonne above futures.

headline: KORYX COPPER HAIB: RECORD 8.01% CU FROM SURFACE, 15 RIGS RUNNING — PFS TARGET Q4 2026
snippet: Koryx Copper (TSXV: KRY) announced August 14 assay results from 17 drill holes (6,430 metres) at the wholly-owned Haib copper porphyry project in southern Namibia, including the highest copper grade recorded at Haib to date: 8.01% Cu and 60.5 g/t Ag from surface in hole HMRC008 (4 to 6 metres). Bulk-tonnage intercepts from the wider program remain the investment thesis: HM155 returned 0.27% CuEq from surface to 831 metres including 244 metres at 0.42% CuEq, while HM139 and HM147 returned 76 metres at 0.52% CuEq and 84 metres at 0.47% CuEq respectively. Koryx now has 15 drill rigs operating at Haib, seven of them on double shifts, as the company pushes toward a Preliminary Feasibility Study targeted for publication at the end of 2026. The Haib porphyry is among the largest undeveloped copper resources in Africa at current drilling scale, and a PFS release at year-end would make it one of the most advanced copper development projects globally at a time when copper is trading above $6.60 per pound and LME backwardation is screaming near-term supply deficit.

headline: SLAM EXPLORATION DRILLS 1.19% CuEq OVER 24.6M AT GOODWIN — NEW CU-NI-CO DISCOVERY 2KM NORTHWEST IN NEW BRUNSWICK
snippet: SLAM Exploration (TSXV: SXL) reported that hole GW26-29 at the Goodwin Copper-Nickel-Cobalt Project in New Brunswick returned 24.6 metres grading 1.19% copper equivalent from the massive sulphide zone — a solid intersect for a Cu-Ni-Co VMS-style target in a Tier 1 Canadian jurisdiction. More significant geologically is the company's concurrent discovery of massive sulphides in hole GW26-36, located 2,000 metres northwest of the Logan Zone — a new target entirely outside the area of known mineralization. SLAM has drilled 2,600 metres in 12 holes across the 2026 program with all 12 holes intersecting host gabbro with variable sulphide mineralization, suggesting the VTEM geophysical targets are consistently predicting mineralized rock. The combination of a 2km lateral discovery outside the known zone and continued confirmation hits in the Logan trend positions the 2026 MRE update as potentially a resource growth story, not a conversion exercise. SLAM received a $60,000 provincial exploration grant from New Brunswick to support the program.

headline: REVIVAL GOLD MERCUR COLUMN LEACH PASSES METALLURGICAL TEST — UTAH HEAP PFS ON TRACK FOR Q1 2027
snippet: Revival Gold (TSXV: RVG) reported August 17 that interim results from 20 column leach tests at the Mercur Gold Project in Utah confirm the amenability of ore to conventional crushed-ore heap leaching — a critical gate for a project that is targeting heap leach as its primary recovery method. The metallurgical program, conducted by Kappes Cassiday & Associates (KCA) in Reno, Nevada, is feeding directly into the Prefeasibility Study (PFS) targeted for completion by end of Q1 2027. Together with extensive available cyanide-soluble assay data, the column results will refine recovery and processing assumptions for Mercur — a project Revival has positioned as Utah's next new operating gold mine. The positive column leach confirmation removes a key technical de-risking milestone from the project's critical path: heap leach metallurgical failure would have been a serious setback, whereas confirmation of amenability is straightforward justification for advancing to PFS. At $4,400 gold, a Utah-jurisdiction heap leach project advancing toward a Prefeasibility Study carries a meaningfully higher NPV than any prior technical studies would reflect.

headline: ASANTE GOLD Q2: 57,274 OZ AT $4,281 AISC — GHANA PRODUCER FACES TIGHT MARGINS EVEN AT $4,400 GOLD
snippet: Asante Gold (TSXV: ASE) reported Q2 2026 production of 57,274 gold equivalent ounces from its Bibiani and Chirano mines in Ghana, with an H1 total of 117,076 ounces — at a consolidated AISC of $4,281 per ounce. At the current gold spot price of approximately $4,400, that leaves a margin of roughly $119 per ounce — a stark contrast to Canadian producers like IAMGOLD (Côté AISC under $1,200) and Alamos Gold (Island Gold under $1,000) that are generating free cash flow yields of 20-30% on enterprise value at the same gold price. Updated NI 43-101 technical reports for Bibiani and Chirano, filed August 5, show combined Measured and Indicated Resources of 4.6 million ounces. The Asante results are a useful reminder that geographic jurisdiction, ore grade, and mining method matter enormously at record gold prices: not every gold producer benefits equally from $4,400 gold, and high-cost operations in challenging jurisdictions remain exposed to operational cost pressures that can effectively neutralise the commodity tailwind. For retail investors evaluating Ghana-listed or West Africa-exposed juniors, Asante's Q2 AISC is a concrete data point on the cost structure of the region's operating mines.

headline: MP MATERIALS SURGES 8%, USA RARE EARTH 9% AS SERRA VERDE VOTE SET FOR AUGUST 28 — $2.83B DEAL DECISION WEEK APPROACHES
snippet: Rare earth equities surged on August 14 with MP Materials (NYSE: MP) up approximately 8% and USA Rare Earth (NASDAQ: USAR) up approximately 9% — moves attributed to both ongoing policy positioning for US tariff and industrial policy support and the approaching August 28 shareholder vote on USA Rare Earth's $2.83 billion acquisition of Serra Verde Group, the only producer outside Asia capable of supplying all four key magnetic rare earths at scale. The MP Materials move was partly a re-rating of its strong Q2 results (revenue $108.49 million, up 89% year-over-year, beating consensus by 13.1%) and a confirmed long-term supply deal for separated gadolinium with a major US aerospace and defence customer. The August 28 USA Rare Earth shareholder vote — on issuing 126.8 million new shares plus $300 million cash to acquire Serra Verde — is the most significant structural rare earth event of the month: if approved, it creates a vertically integrated US and Brazil rare earth producer at a time when China's export restrictions have made supply-chain independence the defining strategic priority for Western defence and industrial policy.

headline: GOLD SPEC LONGS AT 6-MONTH 100TH PERCENTILE — COT DATA FLAGS CROWDING RISK HEADING INTO FOMC WEEK
snippet: The August 14 CFTC Commitments of Traders report shows managed-money gold net longs rising to 217,900 contracts (up from 197,600 the prior week) — positioning that sits at the 100th percentile of its six-month range and the 88th percentile over the past year. Open interest increased by 28,758 contracts, consistent with fresh long participation rather than short covering, which is a technically constructive signal. The risk is crowding: when speculative gold positioning is simultaneously at a six-month maximum and only two weeks away from a binary FOMC catalyst (August 19 minutes) and a larger September rate-decision driver, the structural conditions for a sharp tactical selloff are present even if the medium-term bull case remains intact. Gold fell approximately $80 per ounce in the three trading days after the July 14 FOMC minutes before recovering — a pattern that a 100th-percentile spec-long starting position would amplify. The constructive medium-term read: the fresh-participation interpretation of rising open interest suggests new bulls are entering rather than existing longs adding, which historically supports the next leg after any FOMC-driven correction. For retail investors sizing positions, the COT data argues for caution on leverage into FOMC week.

headline: GOLD MINERS JUST POSTED SECOND-BEST QUARTERLY FUNDAMENTALS EVER — YET EQUITY MULTIPLES STILL BELOW 5-YEAR AVERAGE
snippet: Adam Hamilton's quarterly gold miner fundamentals analysis at GoldSeek finds Q2 2026 results across the major producers tracking as the second-best on record — a remarkable outcome given that gold averaged below $4,400 during the quarter after the January high of $5,600, meaning the second-best earnings quarter came at a gold price well below the cycle peak. Per-mine operating cash flows and all-in sustaining cost margins set records or near-records across the GDX and GDXJ constituent universe. The perverse reality identified in the analysis: despite record earnings, gold miner equity multiples (forward P/E around 11x, EV/EBITDA well below historical averages) remain below five-year averages — implying the sector is generating its best fundamental results at the same time it is priced as if those results are unsustainable. This multiple compression versus earnings growth is the technical foundation for the re-rating thesis: when sector earnings are at record highs and valuation multiples are at five-year lows simultaneously, the gap tends to close via equity price appreciation rather than earnings deterioration. For retail investors evaluating entry timing, the Q2 fundamentals argue that the easy re-rating trade — from distressed-multiple to fair-value-multiple at record earnings — has not yet completed.

headline: PACIFIC RIDGE EXPLORATION KLIYUL COPPER-GOLD PROGRAM UNDERWAY — 2,500M DRILL LAUNCH IN BC PORPHYRY BELT
snippet: Pacific Ridge Exploration (TSXV: PEX) announced that a 2,500-metre drill program has started at its 100%-owned Kliyul copper-gold porphyry project in British Columbia, with two drill programs now simultaneously underway across the company's BC porphyry portfolio. Kliyul sits in the Skeena Arch, a geological terrane in north-central British Columbia that hosts several significant copper-gold porphyry deposits and has been a focus of systematic exploration by multiple companies attracted by the combination of prospective geology and Tier 1 jurisdiction. The 2,500-metre Kliyul program represents the company's primary step to test copper-gold porphyry targets identified through prior geophysical and geochemical surveys. At $6.60 copper and $4,400 gold, a British Columbia porphyry drill program represents some of the most economically compelling exploration ground in the world: the dual-commodity economics of copper-gold porphyries in stable jurisdictions means a discovery at Kliyul would be immediately financeable in today's capital markets.

headline: LODE GOLD FREMONT METALLURGICAL DRILLING STARTS AT CALIFORNIA GOLD MINE — MARIPOSA COUNTY HEAP LEACH TARGET
snippet: Lode Gold Resources (TSXV: LOD) announced August 17 the commencement of metallurgical drilling at its flagship Fremont Gold Mine in Mariposa County, California — a historic producing mine that Lode Gold is advancing toward a revised resource estimate and preliminary economic study. The metallurgical drilling program will provide samples for heap leach amenability testing, establishing the recovery parameters required for a preliminary economic assessment. The Fremont Gold Mine sits in the Mother Lode gold belt of central California, a historically significant district that produced tens of millions of ounces during the 19th and early 20th centuries and is attracting renewed attention from junior developers at $4,400 gold. California gold jurisdiction carries both opportunity (strong geological endowment, US-jurisdiction premium) and regulatory complexity (permitting timelines). The metallurgical drilling initiation represents the specific near-term catalyst that moves Fremont from a geological story toward a PEA-ready project — a step that, if successful, would establish the economic framework for investors to assign a project-stage valuation to the mine for the first time.
